# Introduction

## Project Overview

The Restaurant at Kellogg Ranch (RKR) seeks to better understand how its Facebook marketing efforts can support restaurant awareness and reservations.

## Analytics Objective 3

Analyze Facebook content performance and its potential relationship with restaurant reservations.

::: incremental
- Evaluate Facebook content performance.
- Identify audience engagement patterns.
- Develop data-driven marketing recommendations.
:::

## Importance of the Analysis

Understanding Facebook content performance can help RKR:

::: incremental
- Identify content that resonates with its audience.
- Improve its social media marketing strategy.
- Allocate marketing resources more effectively.
- Support efforts to increase restaurant reservations.
:::

# Literature Review

## Theory of Planned Behavior

The Theory of Planned Behavior (Ajzen, 1991) explains how behavioral intentions are influenced by three factors:

- **Attitudes:** Consumers' perceptions of dining at RKR.
- **Subjective Norms:** Social influences and recommendations.
- **Perceived Behavioral Control:** How easily consumers can make a reservation.

# Methods

## Data and Sampling

- Data source: Collins College Facebook analytics
- Study period: April – October 2026
- Unit of analysis: Individual RKR-related Facebook posts
- Proposed additional source: OpenTable reservation data

## Data Wrangling

::: incremental
- Identify RKR-related Facebook posts.
- Examine missing values and duplicate observations.
- Categorize posts by content type.
- Calculate engagement metrics.
- Prepare datasets for further analysis.
:::

## Analytics Methods

- Descriptive statistics
- Content category comparisons
- Engagement rate analysis
- Content performance rankings
- Correlation analysis, pending reservation data

## Proposed Analytical Measures

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)

measures <- tibble(
  Metric = c(
    "Impressions",
    "Engagements",
    "Engagement Rate",
    "Content Type",
    "Reservations"
  ),
  Purpose = c(
    "Measure content visibility",
    "Measure audience interaction",
    "Evaluate content effectiveness",
    "Compare marketing themes",
    "Measure dining demand"
  )
)

knitr::kable(measures)
```

# Example Analysis

## Facebook Engagement by Content Type (Simulated Data for Practice)

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)

facebook <- tibble(
  Content = c("Menu", "Events", "Student Chefs", "Promotions"),
  Engagements = c(120, 85, 150, 110)
)

ggplot(facebook, aes(x = Content, y = Engagements, fill = Content)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    title = "Facebook Engagement by Content Type",
    x = "Content Type",
    y = "Engagements",
    caption = "Simulated data for demonstration purposes"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
